title: Model Selection Tradeoffs — Choose the Smallest Tool That Does the Job
key_insight: Compare candidates on representative tasks and constraints. A smaller model that meets the quality floor is often easier to serve.
body:
## Choose the Smallest Tool That Does the Job

A large model writes excellent poetry but is used only to classify three ticket types. Its extra ability creates unnecessary cost.

Compare candidates on representative tasks and constraints. A smaller model that meets the quality floor is often easier to serve.

Keep a fallback for cases outside the smaller model’s competence rather than forcing one model onto every request.
common_mistakes: Parameter count alone selects the best deployment.
Hosted and local models have identical privacy responsibilities.
A theoretical speedup guarantees lower production tail latency.
mini_exercise: Draw “Choose the Smallest Tool That Does the Job” as three steps and explain each one.
real_world_usage: Real systems choose among local, hosted, small, and large models by workload-specific constraints.
explain_back_prompt: Use “Choose the Smallest Tool That Does the Job” to explain Model Selection Tradeoffs plainly.
